items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: And I said, “Oh Ruth, that’s terrible to have to do that. Why don’t you just make up your own?”

ctx.x: I never count how much you sing them. But here’s a funny one. We left Ventura at the end of 1949. Then Ruth Price, who runs the Jazz Bakery out in Los Angeles and is doing

very well with it, is also a singer. She joined Ventura after we left, and she said that he had her write down all the syllables on long butcher paper, just sheets of it. And she said she would have it hanging on the walls anywhere she could see it so she could do these charts the same way. And I said, “Oh Ruth, that’s terrible to have to do that. Why don’t you just make up your own?” She says, “no, he wanted just like it was on the original.

And she probably wasn’t used to doing that at that point you know, because she wasn’t singing vocalese. And we’d been doing it. Now it’s easy. Now when we do just an arrangement we sit down and the right thing sort of comes. Once in a while we’ll quibble over you know, we each have a different viewpoint, but then it always comes down to which one works best. But we sort of more or less sing it and fall right into it now. So it’s easier.
